principles.title: Posture before motion
principles.teaching_summary: Set up body position before coordinating the ball movement.
principles.review_question: Is the torso position observable at the beginning of the shot?

principles.title: Hip loading
principles.teaching_summary: Sitting into the hips is discussed as part of the shooting preparation.
principles.review_question: How do the measured hip and knee positions change during the setup?

principles.title: Balance and connection to ground
principles.teaching_summary: Balance and contact with the ground matter to preparation.
principles.review_question: Can feet and body stability be seen before the shooting motion?

principles.title: Vertical versus lateral movement
principles.teaching_summary: The lesson emphasizes directing the body's movement upward rather than adding unnecessary sideways movement.
principles.review_question: What observed direction does the torso/hip center move, given this camera view?

principles.title: Organizing hands and ball
principles.teaching_summary: Before shooting, establish a deliberate shooting-hand and ball relationship.
principles.review_question: Can the ball and shooting hand be tracked together at the set position?

principles.title: Arm/body connection
principles.teaching_summary: The masterclass discusses coordinated arm and torso positioning.
principles.review_question: How does the elbow move relative to the shoulder and torso?

principles.title: Shooting movement sequence
principles.teaching_summary: The shot is taught as coordinated stages, not merely a single joint angle.
principles.review_question: Can ball rise and knee/hip extension be time-aligned?

principles.title: Ball and body timing
principles.teaching_summary: The ball's upward movement is discussed relative to lower-body movement.
principles.review_question: Does the ball begin moving before, during, or after the measurable leg extension?

principles.title: Pre-release ball pathway
principles.teaching_summary: The lesson considers the path of the ball toward release and unnecessary detours.
principles.review_question: How consistent is the observed pre-release ball path?

principles.title: From slow stages to fluid shooting
principles.teaching_summary: Practicing stages slowly before blending them smoothly is presented as a learning process.
principles.review_question: Is a slow-motion set-to-release review appropriate for this player's footage?

principles.title: Release depends on preceding sequence
principles.teaching_summary: Release height and timing are discussed in relation to the preceding motion.
principles.review_question: Where does the release occur relative to the rising body?

principles.title: Ball grip and hand tension
principles.teaching_summary: The lesson discusses hand control and avoiding excess tension.
principles.review_question: Is detailed hand motion visible enough even for a qualitative review?
missing_validation: grip pressure cannot be inferred from pose

principles.title: Controlled backboard shooting progression
principles.teaching_summary: Simple backboard-oriented practice is introduced as a learning exercise.
principles.review_question: Would a controlled practice format suit the player's current skill objective?

principles.title: Dribble-drop shot preparation
principles.teaching_summary: Dribble-drop style practice emphasizes readiness, balance, and timing.
principles.review_question: Does the recording capture the lead-in dribble and plant?

principles.title: Catching into shot preparation
principles.teaching_summary: The masterclass discusses linking the catch and the preparatory motion.
principles.review_question: Can foot readiness, catch, and ball lift be measured from the footage?

principles.title: Close-to-hip starting position in example
principles.teaching_summary: Dunn describes a free-throw setup with the ball near the shooting-side hip/waist as one example.
principles.review_question: Is free-throw setup and ball-to-body distance actually visible?

principles.title: Shooting hand underneath the ball
principles.teaching_summary: Dunn stresses the shooting hand being under the basketball before release.
principles.review_question: Can hand-to-ball contact orientation be inspected?

principles.title: Guide-hand compensation and thumb flick
principles.teaching_summary: Dunn describes some guide-hand thumb flicks as potentially compensating for shooting-hand setup.
principles.review_question: Do close-up frames show the guide-hand action and shooting-hand orientation?

principles.title: Prepare feet before the catch
principles.teaching_summary: Dunn describes preparing the feet before catching the ball for a shot.
principles.review_question: Are the feet set before the ball reaches the hands?

principles.title: Player-specific mechanical diagnosis
principles.teaching_summary: Dunn stresses that coaching must be tailored to the player's habits rather than a universal template.
principles.review_question: Does the suggestion distinguish measurements from diagnosis, with uncertainties?

principles.title: Shooting development across contexts
principles.teaching_summary: The public Ground Up outline progresses from grip, connection and balance to dribble shooting, range, catch/release, and game shots.
principles.review_question: What shooting context and development goal are represented by the clip?

principles.title: Do not impose arbitrary high release
principles.teaching_summary: A recent public coach post emphasizes release height emerging from the preceding shot rather than forcing it higher.
principles.review_question: Can we describe release height without an invented angle or minimum?

measurement_limitations: The current pipeline uses 2D joints and intermittent ball detections, not force plates or 3D biomechanics.
100% pose coverage does not prove pose landmark accuracy.
Hand-to-ball contact and fine thumb action are not measurable from wrists alone.
No auto-correction, ideal elbow angle, or forced set/release position is warranted.
Masterclass notes may contain summary or translation errors; check the linked times.
Some guidance is specific to free throws, training contexts or an individual athlete.
